terminal.saved: Terminal settings saved. Open terminals pick them up when they reconnect.

error.fontSize: Use a font size from 10 to 24.
error.generic: The settings could not be saved. Check the fields and try again.

list.title: Users
list.intro: Each user sees only their own servers, credentials and sessions.

role.title: Role
role.label: Role
role.help: Administrators manage users, instance settings and the audit log.
role.selfHelp: You can't remove your own administrator role.

create.title: New user
create.intro: The user signs in with a temporary password and must choose their own at first sign-in.
create.usernameHelp: 3 to 30 letters, numbers, dots or underscores. It can't be changed later.
create.name: Display name
create.passwordHelp: At least 12 characters. Share it over a safe channel.
create.totpHelp: The user sets it up at first sign-in.

ban.title: Access
ban.self: You can't disable your own account.
ban.enableIntro: The account is disabled: the user can't sign in. Their terminal sessions were left as they were.
ban.disableIntro: Disabling signs the user out everywhere and closes their open terminals at once. Their sessions keep running on the server unless you terminate them.
ban.question: Disable {username}? They are signed out right away and can't sign in until you enable the account.
ban.terminate: {count, plural, =0 {No running sessions to terminate} one {Also terminate their running session} other {Also terminate their # running sessions}}
ban.terminateHelp: Ends the shells on their servers. This can't be undone.

totpReset.title: Two-step verification
totpReset.intro: Resetting removes the user's authenticator and trusted devices, and signs them out everywhere. If two-step verification is required, they set it up again at next sign-in.
totpReset.notEnrolled: The user hasn't set up two-step verification.
totpReset.label: Reset two-step verification…
totpReset.question: Reset two-step verification for {username}? Their authenticator and backup codes stop working.

password.title: Password
password.intro: Sets a temporary password. The user must change it at next sign-in, and is signed out everywhere now.
password.label: Temporary password
password.help: At least 12 characters. Share it over a safe channel.

notice.created: User created. Share the temporary password with them over a safe channel.
notice.enabled: Account enabled. The user can sign in again.
notice.disabled: Account disabled. The user was signed out and their open terminals closed; their sessions keep running.
notice.disabledTerminated: Account disabled. {count, plural, =0 {No sessions needed terminating} one {# session was terminated} other {# sessions were terminated}}.
notice.connectionsOpen: The session service could not be reached, so terminals the user still has open may stay connected for a short while.
notice.terminateFailed: The session service could not be reached, so the user's sessions were not terminated.
notice.passwordReset: Temporary password set. The user must change it at next sign-in.

error.username: Use 3 to 30 letters, numbers, dots or underscores.
error.emailTaken: Another account already uses this email.
error.createFailed: The user could not be created. Check the fields and try again.
error.self: You can't disable your own account.
error.selfRole: You can't remove your own administrator role.

settings.title: Instance settings
settings.intro: Apply to every user of this installation. Each change is recorded in the audit log.
settings.requireTotpHelp: Everyone without it, you included, must set it up before they can continue.
settings.maxHelp: New sessions are refused above this number. Default 50.
settings.localShell: Show local shells (direct mode) to administrators
settings.localShellHelp: Lets administrators add local shells (direct mode) as servers. Their sessions can't start yet: direct mode arrives in a later version.
settings.localShellWarning: When direct mode arrives, local shells will run as the session service's own user, which can read the master key and the database. Leaving this on will then give administrators effective access to every stored credential.

error.max: Use a whole number from 1 to 1000.
error.generic: The settings could not be saved. Try again.

settings.fileTransfer: Allow the file panel (upload and download)
settings.fileTransferHelp: Lets users browse their sessions' servers and upload and download files there, over the session's own SSH connection. Off: the file panel is hidden and the session service refuses file requests.
settings.fileAudit: Record file operations in the audit log
settings.fileAuditHelp: Uploads, downloads, new folders, renames and deletions, with their paths and sizes. File contents are never recorded.

audit.title: Audit log
audit.utc: Dates are in UTC. Times in the table are in your time zone.
audit.caption: Audit events ({total})

files.title: Files
files.keyboardHint: Arrow keys move, Space selects, Enter opens a folder, F2 renames, Delete deletes.

toolbar.label: File actions
toolbar.terminalFolderUnknown: The terminal's folder is known in protected sessions only

path.label: Path
path.invalid: That isn't a path Termdock can open.

list.label: Contents of {folder}
list.name: Name
list.emptyHidden: Only hidden files here. Turn on hidden files to see them.
list.truncated: This folder has more entries than Termdock lists: showing the first {count}.

selection.foldersSkipped: {count, plural, one {# folder was left out} other {# folders were left out}}: folders can't be downloaded yet. Select the files inside instead.

name.dot: “.” and “..” can't be used as names.
name.nul: A name can't contain a null character.
name.tooLong: That name is too long: 255 bytes at most.
name.taken: Something with that name is already here.

delete.title: Delete {items}?
delete.oneFolder: The folder <path>{name}</path> and everything inside it will be deleted from the server. This can't be undone.
delete.foldersWarning: Folders are deleted with everything inside them. This can't be undone.
delete.warning: They will be deleted from the server. This can't be undone.
delete.linksNote: Links are removed as links: what they point to is not touched.
delete.stopped: Stopped after deleting {count, plural, one {# item} other {# items}}.

conflict.title: {count, plural, one {# file already exists} other {# files already exist}} in {folder}
conflict.question: What should happen to them?

drop.title: Drop to upload
drop.foldersSkipped: {count, plural, one {# folder was left out} other {# folders were left out}}: folders can't be uploaded yet.

unavailable.offlineTitle: Files come back when the session reconnects
unavailable.offlineBody: The panel uses this session's connection. Transfers that were running can be retried.
unavailable.tabOfflineTitle: Files come back when Termdock reconnects
unavailable.tabOfflineBody: This browser tab lost its connection to Termdock. It reconnects on its own.
unavailable.sftpTitle: Files need SFTP on this server
unavailable.sftpBody: The panel uses SSH's own SFTP, over this session's connection. The SSH server at <data>{target}</data> didn't offer it. Termdock installs nothing on the server, and the terminal keeps working as usual.
unavailable.sftpSteps: To turn it on, on the server:
unavailable.disabledBody: An administrator turned off file transfer on this Termdock.

proxy.title: A proxy refused the upload of {name}
proxy.body: The proxy in front of Termdock limits the size of uploads (answer 413). Whoever runs Termdock needs to raise that limit: see “Behind a reverse proxy” in the install guide.

error.sessionNotConnected: The session isn't connected. Files come back when it reconnects.
error.filesDisabled: An administrator turned off file transfer.
error.transferExpired: The browser didn't start this download in time. If it asked to allow several downloads, allow them and try again.
error.notFound: It isn't there any more. Refresh the folder.
error.conflict: Something with that name is already here.
error.rateLimited: Too many file operations at once. Wait a moment and try again.
error.forbidden: Not allowed. Sign in again if this keeps happening.
error.connectionLost: The connection to Termdock dropped. Try again once it's back.
error.timeout: The server took too long to answer. Try again.
error.proxyTooLarge: Refused by a proxy: the file is too large for it.
